editorial.headline: Management and Banking Education, With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: Private management and banking courses can be foreign-owned nationally and remain available for PMA registration in Bali at the stated higher-risk large scale.
editorial.body:
This activity is private-sector education in management and banking: the practical, career-facing instruction that turns administrative and commercial subjects into courses. Its scope runs from business, office and health administration through accounting, taxation, insurance, export-import, customs and excise, entrepreneurship, finance, tourism, marketing, banking, capital markets, property, secretarial work and related applied management subjects. It is education with a distinctly operational character, serving learners who need fluency in the machinery of organisations, trade and financial administration.

The register is deliberately broad in subject matter, but its identity is precise: private education or course provision in these fields. A provider may build a curriculum around business management, office practice, banking management or financial and tax administration; it may also focus on specialist commercial skills such as customs, marketing, securities, property or applied management. What holds the activity together is not a single professional outcome, but the delivery of private instruction across the management-and-banking spectrum described in the scope.

Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales are all eligible for this activity. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clean national position: a foreign investor is not dealing with a partial ownership ceiling under this record, but with a fully open ceiling. The applicable PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places its Bali status at OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. In practical terms, a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the route is not barred by the provincial moratorium recorded here. The distinction matters because the national openness is real, and in this case it remains meaningful in Bali rather than being overridden by the island-wide restriction.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today because the provincial moratorium does not block it.
